column1: # OUTSIDE_SPITBOL_BASELINE.tsv -- spitbol_testpgms: programs the ONE ORACLE itself does not run, so they are
# OUTSIDE the graded baseline and OUT OF THE DENOMINATOR. Lon 2026-09-08: the leaderboard divides by the
# programs SPITBOL runs clean, and a program SPITBOL cannot run is recorded per program with SPITBOL's own
# error AND a source check. Written coo 2026-09-08; test_snoflake_suite.sh is the shape.
# MEASURED, not declared: test_snobol4_spitbol_testpgms_suite.sh runs sbl -bf on every program each run and
# cross-checks this file against what it saw, printing STALE (recorded here but sbl answered it cleanly) or
# UNRECORDED (sbl refuses it and this file is silent). UNGRADABLE.tsv mirrors this file row for row and the
# runner says so aloud when the two drift.
# THE SOURCE CHECK IS THE POINT, not decoration: each row quotes the exact statement at the line SPITBOL
# names and says why SPITBOL declines it. Every one of these six is legal SNOBOL4 that SPITBOL refuses on
# environment or on a name collision -- not a program that is wrong. That is what makes it a baseline
# question rather than a defect.
# Oracle: /home/resources/x64/bin/sbl -bf, run 2026-09-08 in a scratch copy with the suite's own testpgms.in.
# Columns: name <TAB> ORACLE_REFUSES <TAB> does not run in SPITBOL: <error, file(line)>; source checked <date> (<who>): stmt <line> <source> -- <why>
test2.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 214 -- bad label or misplaced continuation line, test2.spt(238); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 238 `.                                                          ERROR()` -- a lone period in the label column as a continuation marker; SPITBOL reads column 1 as a label and rejects the line before the program runs. ⛔ NONDETERMINISTIC, and this row corrected itself the same hour: a direct sbl -bf run at 2026-09-08 gave ERROR 214 at line 238, so the first draft of this row claimed the refusal was deterministic -- the very next runner pass got rc=231 with no listing instead. One observation is not a determinism claim. Both paths refuse the program and both put it outside the baseline, which is why the classification is stable even though the symptom is not.

column1: test4.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 116 -- inappropriate file specification for input, test4.spt(65); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 65 `INPUT(.INPUT,,72)` -- a three-argument INPUT association with an EMPTY file specification and a record length; legal SNOBOL4, but SPITBOL requires a real file argument, so it refuses the association rather than the program's logic.

column1: test5.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 116 -- inappropriate file specification for input, test5.spt(6); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 6 `INPUT(.INPUT,,72)` -- the same empty-file-spec association as test4, at the top of the program. Previously graded against a second oracle under CEO-281 clause (2); CEO-391 retires that second oracle, so SPITBOL's refusal is now the whole answer.

column1: test6.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 248 -- attempted redefinition of system function, test6.spt(16); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 16 `DATA('ITEM(COUNT,TOP)')` -- the DATA prototype generates field accessors named COUNT and TOP, and one collides with a name SPITBOL already defines; SPITBOL refuses the redefinition at compile time. The program is valid SNOBOL4 against an implementation whose builtin set does not carry that name.

column1: test7.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 248 -- attempted redefinition of system function, test7.spt(10); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 10 `DATA('SYMB(CHAR,LINK,ALT,ASSOC,SUCC)')` -- same class as test6: the prototype's CHAR accessor collides with SPITBOL's own CHAR, so the DATA statement is refused before execution.

column1: test8.spt
column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 160 -- inappropriate file specification for output, test8.spt(4); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 4 `OUTPUT('TITLE',6,'(14H1THIS IS HAND ,110A1)')` -- an OUTPUT association naming FORTRAN unit 6 with a Hollerith FORMAT string; SPITBOL does not accept that file specification.
